solution.concept: Cause and effect: look for a direct link, a shared trigger, or none
solution.explanation: Each statement is an outcome: the rate decision follows from the central bank's view of inflation and growth, and the jump in air-conditioner sales from hot weather and seasonal demand. Neither explains the other, and no single event explains both. So they are effects of independent causes.
steps: I is a decision (an effect of the monetary-policy assessment)
II is a market outcome (an effect of seasonal heat and demand)
No link between them and no shared trigger: effects of independent causes
solution.why_others_wrong: A common cause would need one event driving both a policy decision and a seasonal sales rise; nothing points to one.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Both the statements I and II are effects of independent causes

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: Several customers of a bank branch have complained that its ATM often runs out of cash on weekends.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action for the bank?

options.text: Shut down the ATM on weekends so that customers stop complaining
Fine customers who withdraw cash from the ATM on weekends
Transfer the branch manager to another branch immediately
Schedule an additional cash refill for the ATM before every weekend

solution.concept: A course of action should solve the stated problem practically
solution.explanation: The problem is a cash shortage on weekends; an extra refill before weekends removes it directly.
steps: Identify the problem: the ATM runs dry on weekends
Choose the action that fixes the cause: more cash before the weekend
solution.why_others_wrong: Shutting the ATM or fining customers punishes users instead of solving the problem; transferring the manager does not put cash in the machine.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Schedule an additional cash refill for the ATM before every weekend

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
In a town, the number of two-wheeler loans sanctioned by banks in October was 30% higher than in September, while the number of two-wheeler loan applications was only 10% higher.

Which of the following can be inferred from this information?

options.text: Banks lowered their interest rates on two-wheeler loans in October
Every application received in October was sanctioned
More two-wheelers were sold in October than in any other month of the year
A larger share of the applications was sanctioned in October than in September

solution.concept: Inference must follow from the numbers given
solution.explanation: If sanctions grew by 30% and applications by only 10%, the ratio sanctions ÷ applications rose (1.3 ÷ 1.1 > 1). So a larger share of applications was approved in October.
steps: Sanction ratio in October = 1.30 S ÷ 1.10 A = 1.18 × (S ÷ A)
So the approval share rose by about 18%
No other option is supported by the data
solution.why_others_wrong: Interest rates and sales across the year are not mentioned; 'every application' is far stronger than the data.
solution.final_answer: Option D: A larger share of the applications was sanctioned in October than in September

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
A coaching institute claims that its students do better in the bank PO exam than other candidates because of its weekly mock tests.

Which of the following, if true, most weakens the institute's claim?

options.text: The institute's mock tests follow the latest exam pattern
Some students of other institutes also clear the PO exam
The institute admits only students who have already scored highly in its own screening test
The institute has branches in ten cities

solution.concept: Weakening a causal claim: find another explanation for the result
solution.explanation: If the institute admits only students who were already strong, their better results may come from that selection rather than from the mock tests, which undercuts the claimed cause.
steps: Claim: mock tests → better results
A weakener offers another cause for the better results
Pre-selecting strong students is such an alternative cause
solution.why_others_wrong: Following the latest pattern supports the claim; other institutes' successes and the number of branches do not touch the cause of this institute's results.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The institute admits only students who have already scored highly in its own screening test

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: The city should build a flyover at the Station Road junction, because it will reduce the time commuters spend waiting in traffic there.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

options.text: The flyover will take three years to build
The city has already built two flyovers elsewhere
Some shopkeepers near the junction oppose the flyover
A traffic study found that most vehicles at the junction go straight through it, which is the movement a flyover would carry

solution.concept: Strengthening: show that the proposed means will produce the claimed effect
solution.explanation: A flyover only saves time for traffic that uses it. If most vehicles go straight through the junction, most of the traffic will bypass the signal, so waiting time falls: this supports the argument.
steps: Claim: flyover → less waiting at the junction
The claim depends on enough traffic using the flyover
Most vehicles going straight confirms that dependence
solution.why_others_wrong: Construction time and shopkeepers' views concern cost or opinion, not the time saved; flyovers elsewhere say nothing about this junction.
solution.final_answer: Option D: A traffic study found that most vehicles at the junction go straight through it, which is the movement a flyover would carry

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
A bank's net profit equals its interest income plus other income, minus operating expenses, provisions for bad loans and tax. This year, Bank A's net profit rose by 20%, although its interest income, operating expenses and tax paid were all exactly the same as last year.

Which of the following must be true?

options.text: Bank A gave out more loans this year than last year
Bank A's provisions for bad loans fell this year
Bank A's other income rose, or its provisions for bad loans fell, or both
Bank A's share price rose by 20% this year

solution.explanation: Profit rose while interest income, expenses and tax were unchanged. The only remaining items in the definition are other income (added) and provisions (subtracted), so at least one of them must have moved in profit's favour. Either alone could explain the rise, so only the combined statement must be true.
steps: Profit = interest income + other income − expenses − provisions − tax
Unchanged: interest income, expenses, tax
So other income rose and/or provisions fell
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Provisions fell' alone need not be true (other income could explain it); more loans would change interest income, which was unchanged; the share price is not linked to the definition.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Bank A's other income rose, or its provisions for bad loans fell, or both

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: Many farmers in a district missed the deadline to enrol in the crop insurance scheme this season because they did not know about it.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Discontinue the crop insurance scheme in the district
Impose a penalty on farmers who miss the enrolment deadline
Remove the enrolment deadline so that no date is ever announced
Publicise the next enrolment deadline well in advance through village panchayats, SMS alerts and local banks

solution.concept: Course of action: address the cause, not the symptom
solution.explanation: The cause was lack of awareness, so spreading information through channels farmers use fixes it directly.
steps: Cause: farmers were unaware of the deadline
Remedy: inform them in time through reachable channels
solution.why_others_wrong: Scrapping the scheme or penalising farmers harms the people it is meant to help; removing the deadline does not make farmers aware and makes the scheme unworkable.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Publicise the next enrolment deadline well in advance through village panchayats, SMS alerts and local banks

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: Since the bank started charging a fee on branch cash deposits above ₹50,000, such deposits at its branches have fallen by 25%. So the fee has succeeded in moving customers to digital channels.

Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

options.text: Over the same period the bank's digital transactions did not increase, while many large depositors moved their accounts to a competing bank that charges no such fee
The fee was announced to all customers by SMS
Digital transactions are cheaper for the bank to process than branch deposits
The fee applies only to cash deposits above ₹50,000

solution.concept: Weakening: show the effect came from a different cause
solution.explanation: The argument assumes the fall in branch deposits means customers went digital. If digital use did not grow and depositors simply left for another bank, the fee drove customers away rather than towards digital channels.
steps: Conclusion: fee → shift to digital
Assumption: the missing deposits went to digital channels
Evidence that they went to a competitor instead breaks the assumption
solution.why_others_wrong: How the fee was announced, why digital is cheaper, and the fee threshold do not show where the deposits went.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Over the same period the bank's digital transactions did not increase, while many large depositors moved their accounts to a competing bank that charges no such fee

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: When a lender's cost of funds falls, it can cut its lending rates without hurting its margin. Over the last two quarters, the cost of funds of most small finance banks has fallen, yet their average lending rates have remained unchanged. In the same period, the share of their loans that turned bad has risen.

Which of the following can most reasonably be inferred from the passage?

options.text: Small finance banks kept lending rates high on purpose to cover their rising bad loans
Small finance banks will cut their lending rates in the next quarter
For most small finance banks, the gap between average lending rates and the cost of funds has widened over the two quarters
Borrowers of small finance banks do not know that the banks' cost of funds has fallen

solution.concept: Inference: what the facts given directly imply
solution.explanation: Lending rates stayed the same while the cost of funds fell, so the difference between the two (the margin on lending) grew. This follows from the facts alone.
steps: Margin on lending ≈ lending rate − cost of funds
Lending rate unchanged, cost of funds down ⇒ margin up
The other options add motives, predictions or knowledge not in the passage
solution.why_others_wrong: The bad-loan motive is a plausible story but is not stated or implied; the next-quarter cut is a prediction; borrowers' awareness is never discussed.
solution.final_answer: Option C: For most small finance banks, the gap between average lending rates and the cost of funds has widened over the two quarters

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: A state government says that waiving stamp duty on home purchases by first-time buyers will significantly increase home ownership among young families in the state.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

options.text: Stamp duty is an important source of revenue for the state government
Most first-time home buyers in the state are young families
Several other states have also reduced stamp duty in the past
Surveys show that the main obstacle for young families is the down payment, which is many times larger than the stamp duty that would be saved

solution.concept: Weakening: show that the proposed means does not remove the real obstacle
solution.explanation: If the real barrier is the down payment, a stamp-duty waiver is too small to change young families' decisions, so home ownership will not rise significantly.
steps: Claim: stamp-duty waiver → more home ownership among young families
The claim assumes stamp duty is a significant barrier
Evidence that the down payment is the main barrier (and far larger) attacks that assumption
solution.why_others_wrong: Revenue loss is a cost argument, not about effectiveness; 'most buyers are young families' supports the argument; other states' actions say nothing about their results.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Surveys show that the main obstacle for young families is the down payment, which is many times larger than the stamp duty that would be saved

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: An internal audit found that several branches of a bank sanctioned loans without verifying the borrowers' income documents, and many of these loans have turned bad.

Courses of action:
I. The bank should make document verification a mandatory step in its loan software, so that a loan cannot be sanctioned without it.
II. The bank should stop all lending until the audit is complete.
III. The bank should investigate the officials responsible and try to recover the bad loans.

Which of the courses of action logically follow?

options.text: All I, II and III follow

solution.concept: Evaluating several courses of action: practical, proportionate, aimed at the problem
solution.explanation: I prevents the lapse from recurring and III deals with the damage already done and with accountability. II is extreme: halting all lending punishes every borrower and branch for a process failure in some.
steps: I: fixes the root cause (missing verification): follows
II: a blanket stop is disproportionate and harms the business: does not follow
III: addresses accountability and recovery: follows
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing II fails because a complete lending halt is out of proportion to the problem; 'Only I' ignores the loans already lost.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only I and III follow
